hypothesis: The DR5 verification wall — that a proposition-ranking nominator cannot distinguish a commitment D from any specific realisation r_i when |realisations(D)| > 1 — is empirically visible in code correctness verification, using a target commitment (naive-UTC datetime handling) that admits multiple non-equivalent surface realisations and three sandboxed Claude verifier subagents blind to labels.

controls.description: Snippets are shipped to verifiers as (id, code) pairs only; ground truth (realisation vs placebo) is committed in snippets.py but never transmitted to a verifier.
Each verifier is prompted to read ONLY the snippets JSON file, no other repository access.
Three verifier subagents run in parallel with no shared context. Consensus is median across the three.
Six gates (W1-W6) with numeric thresholds fixed in DR6_PREREGISTRATION.md before snippets were designed or verifiers spawned.

gates.criterion: All three verifiers produce scores for all ten snippets.
Consensus median score across the five realisations >= 6.
Consensus stdev across the five realisations >= 1.5 (surface-form sensitivity).
Consensus median score across the five placebos <= 3.
At least one placebo receives consensus score >= 5 (projection signal).
